note: Hand-written text for the deck guide pages (deck-*.html and meta-decks.html). build-guides.mjs adds the numbers (field share, core list, matchups, grade) from data.json, meta-cards.json, matchups.json and tests/grade-baseline.json. Every card claim here is read from the card's own text. No em or en dashes.

decks.desc: Mega Rayquaza ex deck guide: Storm Emerald does 50 for every Fire and Lightning Energy you have in play. Core list, game plan and matchups.
decks.title: Mega Rayquaza
decks.lead: Mega Rayquaza ex spreads Fire and Lightning Energy across a board of Pokémon ex, then Storm Emerald does 50 damage for every one of them. It is one of the most played decks in recent online tournaments.
plan: Storm Emerald costs Fire, Lightning and Colorless and does 50 damage for each Fire Energy and each Lightning Energy attached to all of your Pokémon, not only to Mega Rayquaza ex. Every Energy you attach anywhere on your board adds 50. Six in play is 300 damage and seven is 350, enough for nearly any Pokémon in the format.

Most of the deck exists to get that Energy into play quickly. Ethan's Ho-Oh ex's Golden Flame attaches up to two Basic Fire Energy from your hand to one of your Benched Ethan's Pokémon once a turn. Mega Rayquaza ex's Ruler's Roar attaches a Basic Energy from the top 4 cards of your deck to itself when you play it onto your Bench. Crispin finds two Basic Energy of different types, puts one in your hand and attaches the other. Energy Switch then moves a Basic Energy to whichever Pokémon is about to attack.

Mega Kangaskhan ex draws 2 cards with Run Errand while it sits in the Active Spot, and Latias ex's Skyliner gives your Basic Pokémon no Retreat Cost, so you can draw with Kangaskhan and then retreat into Mega Rayquaza ex for free. Talonflame ex puts itself onto your Bench from your hand with Excited Dive while you have a Colorless Mega Evolution Pokémon ex in play, and its Talon Hunt searches your deck for any 2 cards. Legendary Pyroduct turns off the Abilities of Evolution Pokémon in play for both players, which shuts down engines like Drakloak and Meganium while your Basic Pokémon keep theirs.

The cost is prizes. Every Pokémon in the list is a Pokémon ex, and the two Mega Evolution Pokémon ex give up 3 prizes each when they are Knocked Out. The deck has to win the race with big hits rather than trade evenly.
keys: The attacker. Storm Emerald does 50 for each Fire and Lightning Energy on all your Pokémon, and Ruler's Roar gives it a free Energy when you bench it.
Golden Flame attaches two Basic Fire Energy at a time, the fastest way to grow Storm Emerald.
Run Errand draws 2 a turn from the Active Spot. Its own Rapid-Fire Combo is a backup attack for three Colorless Energy.
Skyliner gives every Basic Pokémon free retreat, so you can draw in the Active Spot and still attack with Rayquaza.
A Stadium that turns off Evolution Pokémon's Abilities, which hurts most other top decks more than this one.
Four copies move Basic Energy onto the attacker, so the Energy count is never wasted.
decks.grade: RdyDeck grades winning Mega Rayquaza lists lower than most other top decks. Power reads Storm Emerald as a two hit plan for the biggest Pokémon early in a game, since the full 350 needs seven Energy in play, and every Pokémon in the list gives up 2 or 3 prizes, which costs it on the prize trade. Its online record since Delta Reign is close to even, so the results part of the grade sits near the middle too.

decks.desc: Dragapult ex deck guide: Phantom Dive does 200 and spreads 6 damage counters on the Bench. Core list from top finishes, key cards and matchups.
decks.title: Dragapult
decks.lead: Dragapult ex wins by spreading damage. Every Phantom Dive does 200 to the Active Pokémon and puts 6 more damage counters wherever you like on the Bench. Over the last two sets it has one of the best records of any widely played deck.
plan: Dreepy evolves into Drakloak and then Dragapult ex, a Stage 2 line that most lists play without Rare Candy. That sounds slow, but Drakloak's Recon Directive looks at the top 2 cards of your deck and puts 1 into your hand every turn, so each Drakloak is a draw engine on the way up. Buddy-Buddy Poffin puts two Basic Pokémon with 70 HP or less, like Dreepy, onto your Bench at once.

Phantom Dive costs only Fire and Psychic, does 200 damage, and puts 6 damage counters on your opponent's Benched Pokémon in any way you like. Munkidori's Adrena-Brain moves up to 3 damage counters from one of your Pokémon to one of your opponent's each turn while it has Darkness Energy attached, so damage Dragapult takes comes back out onto the other board. Spread damage sets up turns where one attack Knocks Out the Active Pokémon and a damaged Benched Pokémon together.

Dragapult ex is a Tera Pokémon, so damage from attacks can't hurt it while it is on your Bench. Budew's Itchy Pollen costs no Energy and stops your opponent playing Items from their hand during their next turn, which buys time while your Stage 2 Pokémon come online. Rosa's Encouragement attaches up to two Basic Energy from your discard pile to a Stage 2 Pokémon when you have more Prize cards left than your opponent, so a fresh Dragapult ex can attack right away after one is Knocked Out.
keys: The attacker. Phantom Dive does 200 and spreads 6 damage counters across the Bench for just two Energy.
Recon Directive picks 1 of the top 2 cards every turn, so the evolution line draws as it grows.
Adrena-Brain moves 3 damage counters from your Pokémon to your opponent's, turning spread into knockouts.
Itchy Pollen locks Items for a turn, for free, while you set up.
Benches two Dreepy at once on the first turn, so the line is ready to evolve.
Refuels a new Dragapult ex from the discard pile when you are behind on prizes.
decks.grade: RdyDeck grades Dragapult as tournament ready. Power counts its spread as more than the 200 printed on Phantom Dive, Drakloak's draw keeps Setup speed high without Rare Candy, and most of the list gives up a single prize. Its strong online record adds to the grade.

decks.desc: Basic Box deck guide: only Basic Pokémon, a new attacker every turn and up to 8 on the Bench with Area Zero. Core list, key cards and matchups.
decks.title: Basic Box
decks.lead: Basic Box plays only Basic Pokémon and picks a different attacker every turn. With Area Zero Underdepths and a Tera Pokémon in play it can hold up to 8 Pokémon on the Bench, so the right answer is usually already waiting.
plan: Almost every Pokémon in the list is a Basic, so there is little to evolve and no turn spent waiting. Talonflame ex, in most lists, is the exception: its Excited Dive puts it straight onto your Bench from your hand while you have a Colorless Mega Evolution Pokémon ex like Mega Kangaskhan ex in play. Teal Mask Ogerpon ex's Teal Dance attaches a Basic Grass Energy from your hand to itself and draws a card, Mega Kangaskhan ex draws 2 with Run Errand from the Active Spot, and Latias ex gives every Basic Pokémon free retreat. Area Zero Underdepths lets a player with a Tera Pokémon in play, like Teal Mask Ogerpon ex, have up to 8 Pokémon on their Bench.

The attackers each solve a different problem. Mega Kangaskhan ex, at 4 copies the most played Pokémon in the list, attacks for 200 or more with Rapid-Fire Combo, which costs three Energy of any type. Raging Bolt ex's Bellowing Thunder discards any amount of Basic Energy from your Pokémon and does 70 damage for each one, so it can take one huge knockout. Iron Leaves ex's Rapid Vernier switches it into the Active Spot when you bench it and moves any amount of Energy from your other Pokémon onto it, so it can attack for 180 out of nowhere. Lillie's Clefairy ex's Fairy Zone makes your opponent's Dragon Pokémon weak to Psychic, a tool against Dragapult.

Energy Switch, Crispin and Glass Trumpet keep the Energy moving. Glass Trumpet works while you have a Tera Pokémon in play and attaches a Basic Energy from your discard pile to each of up to two Benched Colorless Pokémon, such as Mega Kangaskhan ex, which turns Energy spent on Bellowing Thunder back into fuel. The price is prizes: nearly every Pokémon gives up 2, and Mega Kangaskhan ex gives up 3.
keys: Teal Dance attaches Grass Energy and draws a card each turn, and it is the Tera Pokémon that turns on Area Zero Underdepths and Glass Trumpet.
Bellowing Thunder does 70 for each Basic Energy you discard from your Pokémon, the deck's biggest single hit.
Rapid Vernier jumps into the Active Spot with all the Energy it needs when you bench it.
Four copies. Run Errand draws 2 from the Active Spot, and Rapid-Fire Combo does 200 or more for any three Energy.
Fairy Zone makes Dragon Pokémon weak to Psychic.
Up to 8 Benched Pokémon while you have a Tera Pokémon in play.
Puts discarded Basic Energy back onto two Benched Colorless Pokémon.
decks.grade: Basic Box grades among the highest decks in RdyDeck. Power is near full because six different Pokémon in a typical list can hit for 170 or more, and its Abilities draw cards every turn. Synergy reads lower than the grade, because a toolbox spreads its cards over many single copies, but that fit check only lowers the grade when the fit is very loose.

decks.desc: Slowking deck guide: stack your own deck so Seek Inspiration copies Kyurem's Trifrost and other big attacks. Core list, game plan and matchups.
decks.title: Slowking
decks.lead: Slowking borrows other Pokémon's attacks. Its Seek Inspiration discards the top card of your deck and, if that card is a Pokémon without a Rule Box, uses one of its attacks. The deck sets up the top of its own deck so it knows what Slowking will copy.
plan: Seek Inspiration costs Psychic and Colorless. Academy at Night lets each player put a card from their hand on top of their deck once during their turn, and Ciphermaniac's Codebreaking searches your deck for any 2 cards and puts them on top in the order you choose. Either way, you decide which Pokémon Seek Inspiration discards.

Kyurem and Metagross are the two copy targets every list plays, 2 copies each. Metagross's Bounce Back does 60 and makes your opponent switch their Active Pokémon to the Bench, and its Metallic Hammer does 150 or more. Kyurem's Trifrost does 110 damage to 3 of your opponent's Pokémon, so two uses through Slowking can Knock Out three Pokémon with 220 HP or less. Trifrost also discards all Energy from the attacking Pokémon. Boomerang Energy helps here: when it is discarded by an effect of an attack used by the Pokémon it is attached to, it is attached back to that Pokémon after the attack. Annihilape's Ghostly Blow and Zeraora's Thunder Raid give Slowking more options in some lists.

Telepathic Psychic Energy searches your deck for up to 2 Basic Psychic Pokémon and puts them onto your Bench when you attach it from your hand to a Psychic Pokémon, which fills the board with Slowpoke on the first turns. Wondrous Patch attaches a Basic Psychic Energy from your discard pile to a Benched Psychic Pokémon. Mega Kangaskhan ex draws 2 a turn from the Active Spot, and Latias ex keeps retreat free for your Basic Pokémon.
keys: Seek Inspiration copies an attack from the Pokémon it discards from the top of your deck.
A copy target in every list: Trifrost hits 3 of your opponent's Pokémon for 110 each. Metagross is the other.
Puts a card from your hand on top of your deck once a turn, so you choose what Slowking copies.
Searches for any 2 cards and stacks them on top of your deck.
Comes back to the attacker after an attack's effect discards it, like Trifrost's.
Benches up to 2 Basic Psychic Pokémon when you attach it to a Psychic Pokémon.
decks.grade: RdyDeck reads the Kyurem copy and counts Slowking as hitting three Pokémon at once. Its main caution for most Slowking lists is that they run no Boss's Orders or Prime Catcher, so the deck can only Knock Out what your opponent puts in the Active Spot, which Trifrost's Bench damage partly makes up for.

decks.desc: Alakazam Dudunsparce deck guide: draw a big hand, then Powerful Hand places 2 damage counters per card. Core list, key cards and matchups.
decks.title: Alakazam Dudunsparce
decks.lead: Alakazam's Powerful Hand places 2 damage counters on your opponent's Active Pokémon for each card in your hand. This deck draws as many cards as it can, and the more it holds, the harder it hits.
plan: Abra evolves into Kadabra and then Alakazam, and both evolutions draw when you play them from your hand to evolve: Kadabra's Psychic Draw draws 2 and Alakazam's draws 3. Rare Candy skips Kadabra when you need Alakazam fast, and Dawn searches your deck for a Basic, a Stage 1 and a Stage 2 Pokémon at once. Dudunsparce's Run Away Draw draws 3 more and then shuffles Dudunsparce and its attached cards back into your deck, so you can play it again later.

Powerful Hand costs a single Psychic Energy. With 11 cards in hand it places 22 damage counters, the same as 220 damage. Enriching Energy, the usual ACE SPEC, draws 4 cards when you attach it from your hand. Because Powerful Hand places damage counters rather than doing damage, Weakness and Resistance don't apply to it.

Alakazam gives up just one prize, so the deck can trade one Pokémon for each two prize Pokémon ex the other side loses. Battle Cage stops damage counters from being placed on Benched Pokémon by the opponent's attacks and Abilities, which protects your Abra and Kadabra from spread like Phantom Dive's.
keys: Powerful Hand places 2 damage counters for each card in your hand, for one Psychic Energy.
Psychic Draw draws 2 when you evolve into it.
Run Away Draw draws 3, then shuffles itself back into your deck to be used again.
Draws 4 cards when you attach it, a big boost to Powerful Hand.
Keeps damage counters off your Bench, a shield against spread decks.
decks.grade: Synergy is close to perfect for this deck: every evolution has its line and the deck draws every turn. Power holds it back a little. RdyDeck estimates Powerful Hand at about 220 from an 11 card hand, which means two hits for the biggest Pokémon ex, though each Alakazam gives up only one prize.

decks.desc: Ogerpon Meganium Hydrapple guide: Wild Growth doubles every Grass Energy and Syrup Storm grows with them. Core list, game plan and matchups.
decks.title: Ogerpon Meganium Hydrapple
decks.lead: This Grass deck puts as many Basic Grass Energy into play as it can. Meganium's Wild Growth makes each one provide two Grass Energy, and Hydrapple ex's Syrup Storm grows with every Grass Energy on your board.
plan: Hydrapple ex is the main attacker, and Teal Mask Ogerpon ex is the engine that can also attack early: Teal Dance attaches a Basic Grass Energy from your hand to it once a turn and draws a card. Its Myriad Leaf Shower does 30 plus 30 for each Energy attached to both Active Pokémon. Hydrapple ex's Ripening Charge attaches another Basic Grass Energy from your hand to one of your Pokémon each turn and heals 30 damage from it.

Meganium and Hydrapple ex are Stage 2 Pokémon, and the list plays no Rare Candy. Forest of Vitality lets Grass Pokémon evolve during the turn they are played, except on a player's first turn, which saves time on both lines. Bug Catching Set looks at the top 7 cards of your deck and takes up to 2 Grass Pokémon or Basic Grass Energy, and Celebi's Traverse Time searches for up to 3 Grass Pokémon and Stadiums for one Grass Energy.

Once Meganium is in play, Wild Growth makes each Basic Grass Energy on your Pokémon provide two Grass Energy. Syrup Storm costs two Colorless and does 30 plus 30 for each Grass Energy attached to all of your Pokémon, so five Basic Grass Energy cards in play make 330 damage. Lana's Aid brings back Pokémon without a Rule Box and Basic Energy from your discard pile for the long game.
keys: The main attacker. Syrup Storm grows by 30 for each Grass Energy on your board, and Ripening Charge adds Energy and heals.
The engine. Teal Dance attaches Grass Energy and draws a card every turn.
Wild Growth makes every Basic Grass Energy provide two Grass Energy.
Lets Grass Pokémon evolve the turn they are played, after your first turn.
Finds Grass Pokémon and Grass Energy from the top 7 cards.
Traverse Time fetches up to 3 Grass Pokémon and Stadiums.
decks.grade: Damage is full marks for this deck, since Syrup Storm can reach 330 with five Grass Energy cards in play. Setup speed is where it loses points: both Stage 2 lines evolve the long way without Rare Candy, so RdyDeck expects them to attack from your third turn. The Setup speed check does not count Forest of Vitality yet, so it may undersell how fast real games go.

decks.desc: Dragapult Dudunsparce deck guide: Phantom Dive spread plus Dudunsparce ex's Tenacious Tail against Pokémon ex decks. Core list and matchups.
decks.title: Dragapult Dudunsparce
decks.lead: A Dragapult ex build that always plays Dudunsparce ex as a second attacker, beside the regular Dudunsparce that draws cards. It has one of the best online win rates in RdyDeck's data over the last two sets, from fewer games than the main Dragapult build.
plan: The core is the same as Dragapult: Dreepy, Drakloak and Dragapult ex, with Buddy-Buddy Poffin to bench Dreepy and Drakloak's Recon Directive to draw on the way up. Phantom Dive does 200 and puts 6 damage counters on your opponent's Benched Pokémon in any way you like, and Munkidori's Adrena-Brain moves damage counters from your Pokémon to theirs.

Dudunsparce's Run Away Draw draws 3 cards and then shuffles Dudunsparce back into your deck. Dudunsparce ex evolves from the same Dunsparce and attacks instead: Tenacious Tail does 60 damage for each of your opponent's Pokémon ex in play for a single Colorless Energy, which hits very hard against decks built from Pokémon ex like Mega Rayquaza or Basic Box. Its Destructive Drill does 150 and is not affected by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

Risky Ruins places 2 damage counters on any Basic Pokémon that is not a Darkness Pokémon when a player puts it onto their Bench during their turn. It hits both players, but it adds to Phantom Dive's spread against decks that bench lots of Basic Pokémon. Poké Pad searches for any Pokémon without a Rule Box, like Dreepy, Drakloak or Dunsparce.
keys: Phantom Dive does 200 and spreads 6 damage counters across the Bench.
Tenacious Tail does 60 for each of your opponent's Pokémon ex in play, for one Energy.
Run Away Draw draws 3 and shuffles itself back in to use again.
Adrena-Brain moves 3 damage counters onto your opponent's Pokémon each turn.
Puts 2 damage counters on most Basic Pokémon a player benches, adding to the spread.
Finds any Pokémon without a Rule Box, which is most of this list.
decks.grade: RdyDeck grades this among the highest of the top decks. Its cards grade the same way as Dragapult's, with spread counted above the printed 200 and Drakloak keeping Setup speed high, and its online record is among the best in the data, which lifts the grade further. The record comes from fewer games than the main build, so the results part counts for a little less.

decks.desc: Dhelmise deck guide: fill your discard pile with Hide 'n' Sneak Pokémon and Vengeful Anchor does 170 for one Energy. Core list and matchups.
decks.title: Dhelmise
decks.lead: Dhelmise's Vengeful Anchor does 170 damage for a single Psychic Energy once you have 4 Pokémon with the Hide 'n' Sneak Ability in your discard pile. The deck fills its own discard pile on purpose.
plan: Shuppet, Banette, Poltchageist and Sinistcha all have Hide 'n' Sneak, which prevents all effects of your opponent's attacks and Abilities on them, though damage still goes through. Gwynn discards up to 2 Pokémon without a Rule Box from your hand and draws 3 cards for each one, so one card fills the discard pile and draws up to 6. Ultra Ball and Prism Tower discard more cards along the way.

With 4 Hide 'n' Sneak Pokémon in the discard pile, Vengeful Anchor does 30 plus 140, so 170 damage. Dhelmise is a Basic Pokémon with 140 HP that gives up one prize. Sinistcha's Matcha Spin places 4 damage counters on each of your opponent's Pokémon once 6 Hide 'n' Sneak Pokémon are in your discard pile, which softens the whole board for Dhelmise. Banette's Puppet Pull does 80 and lets you search your deck for any card.

Telepathic Psychic Energy searches for up to 2 Basic Psychic Pokémon and puts them onto your Bench when you attach it from your hand to a Psychic Pokémon. Every list plays 2 Lillie's Clefairy ex, whose Fairy Zone makes your opponent's Dragon Pokémon weak to Psychic, so Vengeful Anchor does double damage to Dragapult ex. Legacy Energy, the usual ACE SPEC, makes your opponent take one fewer Prize card the first time a Pokémon with it attached is Knocked Out by an attack.
keys: Vengeful Anchor does 170 for one Psychic Energy with 4 Hide 'n' Sneak Pokémon in your discard pile.
Matcha Spin places 4 damage counters on every one of your opponent's Pokémon with 6 in the discard pile.
Puppet Pull does 80 and searches for any card.
Discards up to 2 Pokémon without a Rule Box and draws 3 for each.
Benches 2 Basic Psychic Pokémon when attached to a Psychic Pokémon.
Your opponent takes one fewer prize the first time its Pokémon is Knocked Out.
decks.grade: Synergy is high: the discard plan has every piece it needs. Power reads the deck's best hit as two hits for the biggest Pokémon ex, which still keeps the prize race even, since Dhelmise gives up one prize. Its online record is about even, which keeps the results part of the grade near the middle.

decks.desc: N's Zoroark ex deck guide: Night Joker uses N's Zekrom and N's Reshiram attacks for two Darkness Energy. Core list, game plan and matchups.
decks.title: N's Zoroark
decks.lead: N's Zoroark ex copies attacks. Night Joker uses an attack from one of your Benched N's Pokémon for just two Darkness Energy, so the deck benches N's Zekrom and N's Reshiram and borrows their biggest hits.
plan: Night Joker costs two Darkness Energy and lets N's Zoroark ex use any attack of one of your Benched N's Pokémon. N's Zekrom's Rampaging Thunder does 250 but needs Fire, two Lightning and Colorless Energy on Zekrom itself. Through Night Joker, Zoroark ex only pays its own two Darkness. Rampaging Thunder still stops the Pokémon that used it from attacking during your next turn, so an N's Zoroark ex that copies it has to retreat or sit out a turn. N's PP Up attaches a Basic Energy from your discard pile to a Benched N's Pokémon, and N's Castle gives every N's Pokémon in play no Retreat Cost.

Each N's Zoroark ex in play can use Trade once a turn: discard a card from your hand and draw 2. With two or three on the board, the deck draws deep every turn. Pecharunt ex's Subjugating Chains switches one of your Benched Darkness Pokémon into the Active Spot and makes it Poisoned, and Binding Mochi adds 40 damage to the attacks of the Poisoned Pokémon it is attached to. Black Belt's Training adds 40 more against a Pokémon ex that turn.

Put together, a Poisoned N's Zoroark ex with Binding Mochi copying Rampaging Thunder after Black Belt's Training does 330 damage to a Pokémon ex. Munkidori's Adrena-Brain moves damage counters onto your opponent's Pokémon, and Yveltal is a single prize attacker for when trading two prizes would lose the race.
keys: Night Joker copies a Benched N's Pokémon's attack, and Trade draws 2 a turn.
Its Rampaging Thunder does 250, the attack Zoroark ex copies most, but the copier can't attack during your next turn.
Subjugating Chains switches in a Darkness Pokémon and Poisons it, which turns on Binding Mochi.
Adds 40 damage while the Pokémon it is attached to is Poisoned.
Puts Basic Energy from the discard pile onto Benched N's Pokémon.
Free retreat for every N's Pokémon in play.
decks.grade: RdyDeck counts the copied Rampaging Thunder at 290 for Power, since the full 330 needs both Black Belt's Training and Binding Mochi. Synergy reads lower than most top decks because several lines run single copies, but that only lowers the grade when the fit is very loose. Its online record is about even.

decks.desc: Crustle deck guide: Mysterious Rock Inn stops all damage from your opponent's Pokémon ex attacks. Core list from top finishes, plan and matchups.
decks.title: Crustle
decks.lead: Crustle walls Pokémon ex. Its Mysterious Rock Inn prevents all damage done to it by attacks from your opponent's Pokémon ex, so a deck built around them has to find another way to Knock it Out while Crustle keeps attacking.
plan: Dwebble's Ascension costs one Energy and searches your deck for Crustle, evolving Dwebble on the spot. Attacks from your opponent's Pokémon ex do no damage to Crustle, on the Bench or in the Active Spot. It only stops damage, so attacks and Abilities that place damage counters, like Dragapult ex's Phantom Dive or Munkidori's Adrena-Brain, still work on it, and so does any Pokémon without a Rule Box.

The rest of the list keeps Crustle standing and makes those answers hard to find. Hero's Cape gives it 100 more HP, Growing Grass Energy 20 more, and Jumbo Ice Cream heals 80 from your Active Pokémon once it has 3 or more Energy. Spiky Energy puts 2 damage counters on any Pokémon that damages it in the Active Spot, and Mist Energy prevents the effects of your opponent's attacks on it. Eri discards up to 2 Items from your opponent's hand, and Xerosic's Machinations makes them discard down to 3 cards.

Superb Scissors does 120 and is not affected by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon, so it takes a few turns to Knock Out a big Pokémon. Mega Kangaskhan ex is the other attacker: Run Errand draws 2 cards while it is in the Active Spot, and Rapid-Fire Combo does 200 plus 50 for each heads until you flip tails. It gives up 3 Prize cards when Knocked Out. Team Rocket's Petrel searches for whichever Trainer you need.
keys: Mysterious Rock Inn prevents all damage from attacks by your opponent's Pokémon ex. Superb Scissors does 120.
Ascension searches for Crustle and evolves Dwebble for one Energy.
The ACE SPEC. 100 more HP on Crustle against everything the wall does not stop.
Prevents the effects of your opponent's attacks on the Pokémon it is attached to.
Puts 2 damage counters on any Pokémon that damages the Active Pokémon it is attached to.
Draws 2 a turn with Run Errand and attacks for 200 or more with Rapid-Fire Combo.
decks.grade: Synergy is high, since Dwebble finds its own Crustle and the deck has steady draw. Power is the lower part: Superb Scissors does 120, which takes several hits against the format's biggest Pokémon. Its online record is above even, which lifts the grade a little.

decks.desc: Festival Lead deck guide: with Festival Grounds in play, Dipplin and Seaking attack twice a turn. Core list from top finishes, game plan and matchups.
decks.title: Festival Lead
decks.lead: Festival Lead decks attack twice a turn. With Festival Grounds in play, Dipplin, Goldeen and Seaking may each use an attack twice, and if the first one Knocks Out the Active Pokémon, the second hits the new one.
plan: Dipplin's Do the Wave costs one Grass Energy and does 20 damage for each of your Benched Pokémon, so a full Bench of 5 makes it 100, twice a turn. Buddy-Buddy Poffin and Poké Pad fill the Bench fast, and Festival Grounds has to stay in play for Festival Lead to work, which is why lists run 3 or 4 of it.

Grookey evolves into Thwackey, the engine. Boom Boom Groove searches your deck for any card once a turn while your Active Pokémon has the Festival Lead Ability, and each Thwackey in play can use its own. Seaking's Rapid Draw does 60 and draws 2 cards, and with Festival Lead it does both twice. Rellor evolves into Rabsca, whose Spherical Shield prevents all damage and effects of your opponent's attacks on your Benched Pokémon.

Every bonus to an attack counts twice. Brave Bangle adds 30 damage to each attack against an Active Pokémon ex from a Pokémon without a Rule Box, and Gladion's Final Battle, played as the last card in your hand, adds 80 to each attack that turn. Festival Grounds also keeps any Pokémon with Energy attached, on both sides, free of Special Conditions.
keys: Turns on Festival Lead. Without it in play, nothing attacks twice.
Do the Wave does 20 for each Benched Pokémon, twice a turn.
Boom Boom Groove searches for any card every turn while a Festival Lead Pokémon is Active.
Rapid Draw does 60 and draws 2, twice with Festival Lead.
Adds 30 to each attack against an Active Pokémon ex, up to 60 a turn.
Spherical Shield protects your full Bench from your opponent's attacks.
decks.grade: Power reads close to the top decks, since two attacks a turn with Brave Bangle or Gladion's Final Battle add up fast. Synergy varies more from list to list, because the deck runs two Stage 1 lines and has to keep Festival Grounds in play. Its online record is a little above even.

decks.desc: Mega Excadrill ex deck guide: Maximum Drilling does 330 with two extra Energy, and Metang attaches Metal Energy every turn. Core list and matchups.
decks.title: Mega Excadrill
decks.lead: Mega Excadrill ex hits for 330 once it has two extra Energy attached. Metang's Metal Maker attaches Metal Energy from the top of your deck every turn, so the deck can power it up fast.
plan: Metang's Metal Maker looks at the top 4 cards of your deck once a turn and attaches any Basic Metal Energy there to your Pokémon in any way you like, and each Metang in play can use its own. With about 16 Metal Energy in the deck, a few Metang can load an attacker in one turn. Genesect ex's Metallic Signal searches your deck for up to 2 Evolution Metal Pokémon, like Metang and Mega Excadrill ex.

Drilbur's Call for Family puts up to 2 Basic Pokémon onto your Bench, then Drilbur evolves into Mega Excadrill ex. Maximum Drilling costs 3 Metal Energy and does 200, or 330 if it has at least 2 more Energy attached, enough for most Pokémon ex in one hit. Mega Excadrill ex has 340 HP, and Jumbo Ice Cream heals 80 from it once it has 3 or more Energy. It gives up 3 Prize cards when Knocked Out.

Metang also evolves into Metagross, the second big attacker: Metallic Hammer does 150, or 300 if you discard 3 Metal Energy from it. Energy Recycler shuffles up to 5 Basic Energy from your discard pile back into your deck, where Metal Maker can find them again. Team Rocket's Petrel searches for any Trainer you need.
keys: Maximum Drilling does 200, or 330 with two extra Energy attached. 340 HP.
Metal Maker attaches Metal Energy from the top 4 cards every turn.
Metallic Signal finds 2 Evolution Metal Pokémon at once.
Call for Family fills the Bench and evolves into Mega Excadrill ex.
Metallic Hammer does 300 when you discard 3 Metal Energy.
Puts 5 Basic Energy back in the deck for Metal Maker to find.
decks.grade: Power is among the highest of any deck RdyDeck grades, since Maximum Drilling Knocks Out most Pokémon in one hit. Synergy reads lower and varies more between lists. Its online record is close to even.

decks.desc: Dragapult Dusknoir deck guide: Phantom Dive spread plus Dusknoir's Cursed Blast for 13 damage counters. Core list from top finishes and matchups.
decks.title: Dragapult Dusknoir
decks.lead: A Dragapult ex build that adds Dusknoir. Dusclops and Dusknoir can Knock themselves Out to put 5 or 13 damage counters on any of your opponent's Pokémon, finishing what Phantom Dive starts.
plan: The core is the same as Dragapult: Dreepy, Drakloak and Dragapult ex, with Buddy-Buddy Poffin to bench Dreepy and Drakloak's Recon Directive to draw on the way up. Phantom Dive does 200 and puts 6 damage counters on your opponent's Benched Pokémon in any way you like, and Dragapult ex takes no damage from attacks while it is on your Bench.

Duskull evolves into Dusclops and then Dusknoir. Dusclops's Cursed Blast puts 5 damage counters, and Dusknoir's puts 13, on any 1 of your opponent's Pokémon, and then Knocks Out the Pokémon that used it. That gives your opponent a Prize card, so use it when the Knock Out it sets up is worth more. Duskull's Come and Get You puts up to 3 Duskull from your discard pile back onto your Bench, so the line can be used again.

Budew's Itchy Pollen costs no Energy and stops your opponent from playing Items during their next turn, which buys time while the Stage 2 Pokémon come online. Meowth ex's Last-Ditch Catch finds a Supporter when you put it onto your Bench, and Fezandipiti ex's Flip the Script draws 3 cards on your turn after your opponent Knocked Out one of your Pokémon.
keys: Phantom Dive does 200 and spreads 6 damage counters across the Bench.
Cursed Blast puts 13 damage counters on any of your opponent's Pokémon.
Cursed Blast puts 5 damage counters on any Pokémon, a smaller finisher.
Come and Get You brings up to 3 Duskull back onto the Bench.
Recon Directive picks 1 of the top 2 cards every turn.
Itchy Pollen stops your opponent's Items for a turn, for no Energy.
decks.grade: Its cards grade about the same as the main Dragapult build's. Its online record is close to even, below the main build's, so its grade comes out a little lower.

decks.desc: Dragapult Blaziken deck guide: Blaziken ex's Seething Spirit reattaches Energy every turn for Phantom Dive. Core list from top finishes and matchups.
decks.title: Dragapult Blaziken
decks.lead: A Dragapult ex build with Blaziken ex. Seething Spirit attaches a Basic Energy from your discard pile every turn, so Dragapult ex can attack again soon after it is Knocked Out.
plan: The core is the same as Dragapult: Dreepy, Drakloak and Dragapult ex, with Buddy-Buddy Poffin to bench Dreepy and Drakloak's Recon Directive to draw on the way up. Phantom Dive costs Fire and Psychic, does 200 and puts 6 damage counters on your opponent's Benched Pokémon in any way you like.

Blaziken ex's Seething Spirit attaches a Basic Energy card from your discard pile to 1 of your Pokémon once a turn. The deck plays Fire, Psychic and Darkness Energy, so Blaziken ex can supply one of the two Energy Phantom Dive needs each turn or give Munkidori the Darkness Energy its Adrena-Brain needs to move damage counters. Blaziken ex can attack too: Smolder-sault does 200 for Fire and one more Energy, though it can't attack during your next turn.

Rare Candy takes Torchic straight to Blaziken ex and Dreepy straight to Dragapult ex, skipping the Stage 1. Dawn finds a Basic, a Stage 1 and a Stage 2 Pokémon at once, and Crispin finds 2 Basic Energy of different types, attaching one and putting the other in your hand. Night Stretcher gets back a Pokémon or a Basic Energy from your discard pile.
keys: The main attacker. Phantom Dive does 200 and spreads 6 damage counters across the Bench.
Seething Spirit attaches a Basic Energy from your discard pile every turn. Smolder-sault does 200 as a backup attack.
Adrena-Brain moves 3 damage counters onto your opponent's Pokémon while it has Darkness Energy.
Evolves Torchic or Dreepy straight into Stage 2.
Finds a Basic, a Stage 1 and a Stage 2 Pokémon in one Supporter.
Finds 2 Basic Energy of different types and attaches one.
decks.grade: It grades level with the main Dragapult build, near the top of RdyDeck's grades. Synergy is high, and its online record is one of the better ones in the data.

decks.desc: Sharpedo Toxtricity deck guide: Toxtricity damages your own Mega Sharpedo ex so Hungry Jaws does 270. Core list from top finishes, plan and matchups.
decks.title: Sharpedo Toxtricity
decks.lead: Mega Sharpedo ex hits harder once it is damaged: Hungry Jaws does 120, or 270 if Sharpedo has any damage counters on it. Toxtricity puts those damage counters on it on purpose.
plan: Toxtricity's Sinister Surge searches your deck for a Basic Darkness Energy, attaches it to 1 of your Benched Darkness Pokémon and places 2 damage counters on that Pokémon. Used on a Benched Mega Sharpedo ex, one Ability both powers it up and turns on Hungry Jaws' extra 150 damage. Each Toxtricity in play can use it once a turn, and Toxel's Call for Family benches 2 Basic Pokémon to start.

Pecharunt ex's Subjugating Chains switches one of your Benched Darkness Pokémon, other than a Pecharunt ex, into the Active Spot and makes it Poisoned. Here that helps: Binding Mochi gives the attacks of the Poisoned Pokémon it is attached to 40 more damage against your opponent's Active Pokémon, and Poison adds damage counters between turns, which keeps Hungry Jaws switched on. Mega Sharpedo ex has 330 HP to spare, but it gives up 3 Prize cards when Knocked Out.

Munkidori's Adrena-Brain moves up to 3 damage counters from one of your Pokémon to one of your opponent's while it has Darkness Energy attached, so damage Sharpedo takes can be passed on. Tatsugiri's Attract Customers finds a Supporter from the top 6 cards while it is in the Active Spot, and Sharpedo's own Greedy Fang does 70 and draws 2 cards for one Energy.
keys: Hungry Jaws does 270 once it has any damage counters on it. 330 HP.
Sinister Surge attaches Darkness Energy and 2 damage counters, turning Hungry Jaws on.
Subjugating Chains switches in a Darkness Pokémon and Poisons it.
Attacks from the Poisoned Pokémon it is attached to do 40 more damage.
Adrena-Brain moves 3 damage counters from your Pokémon to your opponent's.
Attract Customers finds a Supporter from the top 6 cards.
decks.grade: RdyDeck grades it a little below most top decks. Synergy is solid, and Power is the lower part. Its online record is close to even.

decks.desc: Talonflame Dusknoir deck guide: Mega Kangaskhan ex lets Talonflame ex dive onto the Bench, and Cursed Blast adds 130. Core list, game plan, matchups.
decks.title: Talonflame Dusknoir
decks.lead: Talonflame ex is a Stage 2 Pokémon this deck never evolves. Its Excited Dive Ability puts it straight onto your Bench from your hand once you have a Colorless Mega Evolution Pokémon ex in play, and Mega Kangaskhan ex is that Pokémon. Dusknoir's Cursed Blast adds 13 damage counters wherever the deck needs them.
plan: Mega Kangaskhan ex is a Basic Pokémon, so it can start in the Active Spot. Its Run Errand draws 2 cards once during your turn while it is in the Active Spot, and Latias ex's Skyliner gives your Basic Pokémon no Retreat Cost, so Kangaskhan can draw and then move to the Bench for free.

Talon Hunt costs 2 Colorless Energy, does 150 and lets you search your deck for up to 2 cards. Ignition Energy provides 3 Colorless Energy on an Evolution Pokémon, so one attachment powers Talon Hunt, but it is discarded at the end of your turn. Hilda searches for an Evolution Pokémon and an Energy card at once, which finds Talonflame ex and Ignition Energy together.

Duskull, Dusclops and Dusknoir come out through Rare Candy, Buddy-Buddy Poffin and Dawn, which searches for a Basic, a Stage 1 and a Stage 2 Pokémon. Dusknoir's Cursed Blast puts 13 damage counters, and Dusclops's puts 5, on any of your opponent's Pokémon, then Knocks Out the Pokémon that used it, which gives your opponent a Prize card. Bloodmoon Ursaluna ex is the late game hitter: Blood Moon does 240 and costs 1 less Energy for each Prize card your opponent has taken.
keys: Excited Dive puts it onto your Bench from your hand. Talon Hunt does 150 and searches for 2 cards.
The Colorless Mega Evolution Pokémon ex that turns on Excited Dive. Run Errand draws 2 a turn.
Provides 3 Colorless Energy on an Evolution Pokémon for one turn, enough for Talon Hunt.
Cursed Blast puts 13 damage counters on any of your opponent's Pokémon.
Searches for an Evolution Pokémon and an Energy card, such as Talonflame ex and Ignition Energy.
Skyliner gives your Basic Pokémon no Retreat Cost, so Kangaskhan can draw and step back.
decks.grade: RdyDeck counts the deck's hardest hit as Bloodmoon Ursaluna ex's Blood Moon with Dusknoir's Cursed Blast added, and counts Mega Kangaskhan ex for its Run Errand draw, not its attack. Rare Candy and four Kangaskhan keep the setup and the draw steady. The deck's online record since Delta Reign is a little under even, which holds the grade below the top decks.

decks.desc: Lopunny Dudunsparce deck guide: Gale Thrust hits for 230 when Mega Lopunny ex moves up from the Bench. Core list, Dudunsparce draw and matchups.
decks.title: Lopunny Dudunsparce
decks.lead: Mega Lopunny ex attacks for a single Energy. Its Gale Thrust does 230 on a turn it moves from your Bench to the Active Spot, and Dudunsparce draws the cards that set that up. Both of its attacks cost only Colorless Energy, so any Energy powers them.
plan: Gale Thrust costs 1 Colorless Energy and does 60, plus 170 more if Mega Lopunny ex moved from your Bench to the Active Spot this turn. Retreating your Active Pokémon into Lopunny does that, and Air Balloon makes the Retreat Cost 2 Colorless less. Spiky Hopper does 160 for 2 Energy, and no effect on your opponent's Active Pokémon changes that damage.

Dunsparce evolves into Dudunsparce, whose Run Away Draw draws 3 cards and then shuffles Dudunsparce and its cards back into your deck, so the same Pokémon can draw again later. Most lists add a Dudunsparce ex, whose Tenacious Tail does 60 for each of your opponent's Pokémon ex in play. Fan Rotom's Fan Call searches for up to 3 Colorless Pokémon with 100 HP or less on your first turn.

Mist Energy prevents all effects of your opponent's attacks done to the Pokémon it is attached to, and Battle Cage stops damage counters being put on Benched Pokémon by your opponent's attacks and Abilities, which blunts attacks that spread damage counters. Wally's Compassion heals all damage from a Mega Evolution Pokémon ex and returns its Energy to your hand.
keys: Gale Thrust does 230 for 1 Energy on the turn it moves up from your Bench.
Run Away Draw draws 3, then shuffles itself back into your deck.
Cuts Retreat Cost by 2 Colorless, so retreating into Lopunny costs little.
Prevents the effects of your opponent's attacks on the Pokémon it is attached to.
Stops your opponent's attacks and Abilities from putting damage counters on your Bench.
Heals all damage from Mega Lopunny ex and puts its Energy back in your hand.
decks.grade: RdyDeck counts Gale Thrust at its full 230 when a list has enough cards to switch Lopunny in or retreat for free. It still grades Lopunny Dudunsparce lower than most top decks, because 230 takes two hits against the format's biggest Pokémon while Mega Lopunny ex gives up 3 prizes when it is Knocked Out. Dudunsparce's draw every turn counts in its favor.

decks.desc: Mega Lucario deck guide: Aura Jab reloads Fighting Energy from the discard pile, then Mega Brave hits for 270. Core list, Lunatone draw and matchups.
decks.title: Mega Lucario
decks.lead: Mega Lucario ex alternates between two attacks. Aura Jab does 130 and puts Fighting Energy from your discard pile onto your Bench, and Mega Brave does 270 for two Energy. Lunatone and Solrock keep the hand full and the discard pile stocked.
plan: Riolu evolves into Mega Lucario ex. Aura Jab costs 1 Fighting Energy, does 130 and attaches up to 3 Basic Fighting Energy cards from your discard pile to your Benched Pokémon in any way you like, so the next attacker is ready. Mega Brave costs 2 Fighting Energy and does 270, but Mega Lucario ex can't use it again during your next turn. Premium Power Pro adds 30 damage to your Fighting Pokémon's attacks on the Active Pokémon that turn.

Lunatone's Lunar Cycle draws 3 cards when Solrock is in play and you discard a Basic Fighting Energy card from your hand, which also loads the discard pile for Aura Jab. Fighting Gong searches for a Basic Fighting Energy card or a Basic Fighting Pokémon, which covers Riolu, Lunatone, Solrock and Energy.

Solrock's Cosmic Beam does 70, not changed by Weakness or Resistance, while Lunatone is on your Bench. Most lists play Gravity Mountain, which gives every Stage 2 Pokémon in play 30 less HP, and Rocky Fighting Energy, which prevents the effects of your opponent's attacks on the Fighting Pokémon it is attached to.
keys: Aura Jab does 130 and reloads 3 Fighting Energy. Mega Brave does 270.
Lunar Cycle draws 3 with Solrock in play, discarding a Fighting Energy for Aura Jab.
Turns on Lunar Cycle. Cosmic Beam does 70 with Lunatone on the Bench.
Fighting attacks do 30 more to the Active Pokémon this turn.
Searches for a Basic Fighting Energy card or a Basic Fighting Pokémon.
Every Stage 2 Pokémon in play gets 30 less HP.
decks.grade: RdyDeck counts Mega Brave with Premium Power Pro as a 300 damage hit, which takes most Pokémon in one hit and the biggest in two. Mega Lucario ex gives up 3 prizes, so the grade marks the trade against those biggest Pokémon as costly. Its online record since Delta Reign is better than over the whole two set window.

decks.desc: Rocket's Honchkrow deck guide: discard Team Rocket Supporters for 60 each with Rocket Feathers, all single prize Pokémon. Core list and matchups.
decks.title: Rocket's Honchkrow
decks.lead: A Team Rocket deck of single prize Pokémon. Team Rocket's Honchkrow does 60 damage for each Team Rocket Supporter you discard from your hand, and most of the Trainers in the list either are those Supporters or find them.
plan: Team Rocket's Murkrow evolves into Team Rocket's Honchkrow. Rocket Feathers costs 2 Colorless Energy and lets you discard any number of Supporter cards with Team Rocket in their name from your hand, doing 60 damage for each. Ignition Energy provides 3 Colorless Energy on an Evolution Pokémon for one turn, and Team Rocket's Energy provides 2 Energy but can only be attached to a Team Rocket's Pokémon.

The list plays 4 each of Team Rocket's Archer, Ariana, Giovanni, Petrel and Proton. Team Rocket's Transceiver searches for one of them, Roto-Stick takes any Supporters from the top 4 cards of your deck, and Team Rocket's Factory draws 2 cards each turn you play a Team Rocket Supporter. Ariana draws until you have 8 cards in hand if all of your Pokémon in play are Team Rocket's Pokémon. Miracle Headset, the ACE SPEC, puts 2 Supporters from your discard pile back into your hand.

Team Rocket's Porygon2 is the second attacker: R Command does 20 damage for each Team Rocket Supporter in your discard pile, so it grows as Rocket Feathers fills the pile. Team Rocket's Articuno prevents the effects of your opponent's attacks on your Basic Team Rocket's Pokémon, and Team Rocket's Giovanni switches your Active Team Rocket's Pokémon with a Benched one, then switches in one of your opponent's Benched Pokémon.
keys: Rocket Feathers does 60 for each Team Rocket Supporter you discard from your hand.
R Command does 20 for each Team Rocket Supporter in your discard pile.
Searches your deck for a Supporter with Team Rocket in its name.
Draws 2 cards each turn you play a Team Rocket Supporter.
Draws to 5 cards, or to 8 when all your Pokémon in play are Team Rocket's.
Repelling Veil shields your Basic Team Rocket's Pokémon from attack effects.
decks.grade: Rocket's Honchkrow gets one of the highest Synergy readings in RdyDeck, because nearly every card supports the Team Rocket Supporter plan. Power is lower: the grade counts Porygon2's R Command as the hardest hit and treats its full damage as a late game plan, since it grows only as Supporters reach the discard pile. Every Pokémon gives up a single prize, so your opponent needs six Knock Outs to win.

decks.desc: Greninja ex deck guide: Shinobi Blade does 170 and searches any card, Mirage Barrage hits 2 Pokémon for 120. Core list, Dusknoir support, matchups.
decks.title: Greninja
decks.lead: Greninja ex is a Stage 2 attacker that finds a card every time it hits. Shinobi Blade does 170 for one Water Energy and searches your deck for any card, and Mirage Barrage does 120 damage to each of two Pokémon. A Dusknoir line and a few Mega Evolution Pokémon back it up.
plan: Froakie evolves into Frogadier and then Greninja ex, usually through Rare Candy or Grand Tree, the ACE SPEC Stadium that lets each player evolve a Basic Pokémon into its Stage 1 and then its Stage 2 straight from the deck once a turn. Frogadier's Summoning Jutsu attack searches your deck for up to 3 Pokémon for one Water Energy. Colress's Tenacity searches for a Stadium and an Energy card, which finds Grand Tree.

Shinobi Blade costs 1 Water Energy, does 170 and lets you search your deck for a card and put it into your hand. Mirage Barrage costs Water and 2 Colorless, discards 2 Energy from Greninja ex and does 120 damage to 2 of your opponent's Pokémon. Ignition Energy provides 3 Colorless Energy on an Evolution Pokémon for one turn, so Water Energy plus Ignition Energy pays for Mirage Barrage.

Dusknoir's Cursed Blast puts 13 damage counters on any of your opponent's Pokémon and then Knocks Out Dusknoir, which finishes what Greninja ex starts. Most lists also play Mega Froslass ex and Mega Starmie ex, whose Nebula Beam does 210 not changed by Weakness, Resistance or effects on the Active Pokémon. Budew's Itchy Pollen stops your opponent from playing Items during their next turn.
keys: Shinobi Blade does 170 and searches for any card. Mirage Barrage hits 2 Pokémon for 120.
Its Summoning Jutsu attack searches your deck for up to 3 Pokémon.
Evolves a Basic Pokémon to Stage 1 and then Stage 2 from your deck, once a turn.
Cursed Blast puts 13 damage counters on any of your opponent's Pokémon.
Provides 3 Colorless Energy on an Evolution Pokémon for one turn.
Nebula Beam does 210, not changed by Weakness, Resistance or effects.
decks.grade: RdyDeck grades Greninja lower than most top decks. Its hardest hit comes from Mega Starmie ex with Dusknoir's Cursed Blast added, and the grade notes that the biggest Pokémon in the format take two hits. Synergy reads lower than in most decks, and its online record since Delta Reign is a little under even.

decks.desc: Ogerpon Meganium Arboliva deck guide: Wild Growth doubles Grass Energy for Myriad Leaf Shower, and Arboliva ex spreads damage. Core list and matchups.
decks.title: Ogerpon Meganium Arboliva
decks.lead: This Grass deck shares its engine with Ogerpon Meganium Hydrapple: Teal Mask Ogerpon ex attaches Grass Energy every turn and Meganium's Wild Growth makes each Basic Grass Energy provide two. Arboliva ex takes Hydrapple ex's place as the second attacker.
plan: Teal Mask Ogerpon ex is the main attacker. Teal Dance attaches a Basic Grass Energy from your hand to it once a turn and draws a card, and Myriad Leaf Shower does 30 plus 30 for each Energy attached to both Active Pokémon. With Meganium in play, each Basic Grass Energy provides two Grass Energy and counts twice, so four Basic Grass Energy on Ogerpon make 270 before counting the Energy on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

Arboliva ex is a 310 HP Stage 2 Pokémon that evolves from Dolliv and Smoliv. Oil Salvo costs one Grass Energy and does 20 damage six times to your opponent's Pokémon, split any way you like, and that damage is not affected by Weakness or Resistance. Aroma Shot does 160 for three Colorless and recovers Arboliva ex from all Special Conditions, and Dolliv's Nutrients heals 40 damage from one of your Pokémon.

Meganium and Arboliva ex are both Stage 2 Pokémon and the list plays no Rare Candy. Forest of Vitality lets Grass Pokémon evolve during the turn they are played, except on a player's first turn, and Dawn searches your deck for a Basic Pokémon, a Stage 1 Pokémon and a Stage 2 Pokémon. Bug Catching Set takes Grass Pokémon and Basic Grass Energy from the top 7 cards, Meowth ex's Last-Ditch Catch finds a Supporter when you bench it, and with Briar you take one more Prize card when Teal Mask Ogerpon ex, a Tera Pokémon, knocks out your opponent's Active Pokémon while they have exactly 2 Prize cards left.
keys: Oil Salvo spreads 120 damage across your opponent's Pokémon for one Energy.
Teal Dance attaches Grass Energy and draws a card, and Myriad Leaf Shower grows with every Energy.
Wild Growth makes every Basic Grass Energy provide two Grass Energy.
Lets Grass Pokémon evolve the turn they are played, after your first turn.
Finds a Basic, a Stage 1 and a Stage 2 Pokémon with one card.
Finds Grass Pokémon and Grass Energy from the top 7 cards.
decks.grade: RdyDeck counts Myriad Leaf Shower as the main hit, reaching 330 with four Basic Grass Energy on Teal Mask Ogerpon ex and two Energy on your opponent's Active Pokémon, and it counts Aroma Shot for Arboliva ex. Setup speed loses points the same way as the Hydrapple build, since both Stage 2 lines evolve the long way without Rare Candy. Synergy loses a little for the number of single copies, and the deck's record above even over the last two sets lifts its grade.

decks.desc: Okidogi Barbaracle deck guide: Prism Energy turns on Adrena-Power for a 230 HP Okidogi doing 170 damage. Core list, game plan and matchups.
decks.title: Okidogi Barbaracle
decks.lead: A Fighting deck built around Okidogi, a Basic Pokémon that becomes a 230 HP attacker doing 170 damage once it has Darkness Energy attached. Every Pokémon in the core list gives up only one Prize card, so your opponent has to take six Knock Outs.
plan: Okidogi's Adrena-Power gives it +100 HP and makes its attacks do 100 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon while it has any Darkness Energy attached. Prism Energy provides every type of Energy while attached to a Basic Pokémon, one at a time, so one Prism Energy turns Adrena-Power on, and the ACE SPEC Legacy Energy does the same. With Adrena-Power on, Good Punch does 170 for two Fighting Energy.

Barbaracle's Stone Arms attaches a Basic Fighting Energy from your hand to one of your Fighting Pokémon once a turn, on top of your normal attachment. Lunatone's Lunar Cycle discards a Basic Fighting Energy from your hand to draw 3 cards while you have Solrock in play, and Solrock's Cosmic Beam does 70 for one Fighting Energy, not affected by Weakness or Resistance, as long as Lunatone is on your Bench. Fighting Gong finds a Basic Fighting Energy or a Basic Fighting Pokémon, and Poké Pad finds any Pokémon without a Rule Box.

Bloodmoon Ursaluna's Battle-Hardened attaches up to 2 Basic Fighting Energy from your hand when you bench it, and Mad Bite does 100 plus 30 for each damage counter on your opponent's Active Pokémon, which finishes big Pokémon that Okidogi has already hit. Battle Cage stops the effects of attacks and Abilities from your opponent's Pokémon from placing damage counters on Benched Pokémon, so attacks like Phantom Dive can't put damage counters on your Bench while it is in play.
keys: Adrena-Power adds 100 HP and 100 damage once Darkness Energy is attached.
Provides every type on a Basic Pokémon, which turns on Adrena-Power.
Stone Arms attaches an extra Basic Fighting Energy each turn.
Cosmic Beam does 70 for one Energy, ignoring Weakness and Resistance, with Lunatone on the Bench.
Lunar Cycle discards a Basic Fighting Energy to draw 3 with Solrock in play.
Stops your opponent's attack and Ability effects from putting damage counters on the Bench.
decks.grade: RdyDeck expects this deck to need two hits for the biggest Pokémon in the format, with Bloodmoon Ursaluna's Mad Bite as its hardest single hit. Every Pokémon gives up one Prize card, so the trade stays even against decks of Pokémon ex. Synergy loses points for spreading the Pokémon over many lines with several single copies, and the deck's record above even since Delta Reign lifts its grade over what the cards alone earn.
